summary_paragraph: A male patient with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis and a history of coronary artery disease was admitted for recurrent chest pain occurring on dialysis days and at rest, relieved by nitroglycerin. Evaluation revealed no acute ischemic changes on EKG or troponin, but due to worsening symptoms, he underwent cardiac catheterization which showed a 90% stenosis in the proximal right coronary artery. Two drug-eluting stents were successfully placed. He remained stable post-procedure, received a scheduled hemodialysis session, and was discharged home with instructions to continue dual antiplatelet therapy, monitor weight, and follow up with cardiology. No complications occurred during the hospital stay.
problems: Coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery
Chronic total occlusion of coronary artery
